entries.summary: Bearish elevated downside risk persists, but Thursday's recovery from the opening selloff and sector rotation limit confidence in a broad immediate breakdown. AP reports Nasdaq +0.2%, S&P +0.2%, Dow +0.3%, NVDA -4.7%, 10Y near 5.10%, and Brent $94.47; exact simultaneous quote times are not established. MarketWatch reports SOX +0.9% during the recovery, also asynchronous. No new curated Open Watch event (159 total). Fresh matched QQQ/SOX, 2Y, VXN/VIX, advance-decline breadth and live FedWatch remain unavailable. Friday PPI remains the next major scheduled catalyst.
bullish: AP reports Nasdaq recovering from an intraday decline as large as 1.6% to +0.2%; the broad market did not sustain the opening breakdown.
MarketWatch reports SOX +0.9% after recovering earlier losses; Reuters reports AMD and AVGO gains, suggesting chip rotation rather than indiscriminate liquidation.
Foxconn and Siemens demand/backlog data support AI infrastructure spending, but do not prove an immediate stock-market response.
bearish: NVDA remains about 4.7% lower in AP reporting after the confirmed leadership transition; governance, financing and export scrutiny remain elevated.
10Y yield near 5.10% and Brent near $94.47 (AP) suggest valuation/inflation headwinds; the matching 2Y yield is unavailable.
Nebius revenue-guidance reduction tied to capacity delays highlights execution and financing risk; Friday PPI could amplify rates pressure.

editorial.marketOverview: Thursday's market absorbed a major Nvidia governance shock without sustaining the opening Nasdaq selloff. AP reported the Nasdaq up around 0.2% after an intraday loss as large as 1.6%, while Nvidia remained roughly 4.7% lower. MarketWatch separately reported SOX up 0.9%. These are different reporting windows and should not be combined into a precise semiconductor-relative-strength measurement.
editorial.whatChanged: Compared with the 12:44 ET assessment, later reporting reinforces the intraday recovery: AP describes a positive Nasdaq and MarketWatch a recovering semiconductor index. The curated Open Watch file is still at 159 events, last updated 18:42:42 UTC, with no newly curated catalyst. This reduces conviction in an immediate market-wide collapse but does not resolve the Nvidia leadership shock or Friday's inflation risk.
editorial.marketInterpretation: The tape looks more like selective repricing and rotation than uniform AI capitulation. Gains in competing chipmakers offset some Nvidia weakness, while elevated yields and oil can still pressure duration-sensitive growth shares. A rounded 10Y yield near 5.10% is not a synchronized Treasury-curve observation; the prior dashboard spread of +24.5bp is historical only.
editorial.threeDayPath: Thursday's closing breadth and SOX-versus-QQQ leadership are the first test. Friday's 08:30 ET PPI could either relieve or reinforce rate pressure; a benign print with semiconductor stabilization offers a relief path, whereas a hot print could trigger renewed downside. Monday tests whether the sector rotation broadens into a sustainable recovery or reverses.
editorial.bullCase: AI infrastructure demand signals from Foxconn and Siemens, positive chipmaker rotation, and a resilient Nasdaq could support a broadening rebound if yields stabilize and PPI is benign. Confirmation requires synchronized closing QQQ/SOX, breadth and volatility evidence.
editorial.bearCase: Nvidia's leadership transition, AI infrastructure execution concerns and a roughly 5.10% 10Y yield leave growth valuations exposed. A hot PPI, rising oil and renewed semiconductor underperformance could reaccelerate downside into Monday.
editorial.watchNext: Verify the Thursday cash close for QQQ, SOX, NVDA, VXN/VIX and advance-decline breadth; compare matched 10Y/2Y yields and live FedWatch. Monitor Cisco/Applied Materials earnings, Friday October PPI and Monday follow-through. Do not interpret forecast impacts as realized market reactions.
